ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r2.claim: The question about fearing God portrays Pharaoh and his people as extremely rebellious; the author paraphrases it as an uncontrolled rise in injustice without fear of God's wrath.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r2.anchor: Will these unjust people continue to increase in their rebelliousness in an uncontrolled manner and not fear God’s wrath?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r3.claim: This warning style conveys anger, yearning, rebuke, and the nearness of God's punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r3.anchor: Anger, yearning, rebuke and the proximity of God’s scourge found in this style does not need any elaboration.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r4.claim: The author says other prophets warn their peoples in the same way later in this sūra.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r4.anchor: It will become evident from verses 125, 143, 162 and 178 ahead that other prophets too warned their nations in this way.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r16.claim: The people are wrongdoers because they disbelieved and oppressed Israelites through enslavement and killing their sons.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r16.anchor: وسجل عليهم بالظلم، لظلم أنفسهم بالكفر، وظلم بني إسرائيل بالاستعباد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r17.speaker: وقيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r17.claim: An unnamed grammatical view parses “people of Pharaoh” as a badal for “the wrongdoers.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r17.anchor: وقوم فرعون، وقيل: بدل من القوم الظالمين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r18.claim: The author prefers apposition: both expressions identify the same people, and the more familiar “Pharaoh's people” removes ambiguity in “the wrongdoers.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r18.anchor: والأجود أن يكون عطف بيان لأنهما عبارتان يعتقبان على مدلول واحد، إذ كل واحد عطف البيان،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r19.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r19.claim: The majority read ألا يتقون with a third-person yāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r19.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ألا يتقون، بالياء على الغيبة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r20.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم بن يسار، وشقيق بن سلمة، وحماد بن سلمة، وأبو قلابة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r20.claim: These readers use second-person tāʾ as an abrupt address to absent Pharaoh's people, rebuking them through the message delivered to them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r20.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن مسلم بن يسار، وشقيق بن سلمة، وحماد بن سلمة، وأبو قلابة: بتاء الخطاب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r21.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r21.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the reading means “tell them”; the phrasing both denies that they fear God and commands them to do so.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r21.anchor: قال ابن عطية: معناه قل لهم، فجمع في هذه العبارة من المعاني نفي التقوى عنهم وأمرهم بالتقوى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads ألا يتقون as a fresh remark after the sending, expressing Moses' astonishment at their oppression, confidence, and lack of fear of God's days.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r1.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: بم تعلق قوله: ألا يتقون؟ قلت: هو كلام مستأنف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r2.claim: He also allows a circumstantial clause referring to the wrongdoers: they oppress without fearing God or His punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ألا يتقون حالا من الضمير في الظالمين، أي يظلمون غير متقين الله وعقابه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r3.claim: The author rejects that parse: it separates the governor from its dependent with “Pharaoh's people,” and a clause after the interrogative hamza cannot be governed from before it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r3.anchor: وهذا الاحتمال الذي أورده خطأ فاحش لأنه جعله حالا من الضمير في الظالمين، وقد أعرب هو قوم فرعون عطف بيان،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r4.claim: A reading with fatḥa or kasra on the nūn is explained as أفلا يتقونني, with the nūn and first-person yāʾ elided to avoid adjacent sukūns.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r4.anchor: وقرىء: بفتح النون وكسرها، التقدير: أفلا يتقونني؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers ألا يا ناس اتقون as another parse, comparing ألا يسجدوا and positing loss of the yāʾ alif in speech and writing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r5.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: في ألا يتقون بالياء وكسر النون وجه آخر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r6.claim: The author calls that derivation far-fetched and prefers ألا as an exhortative particle urging piety, rejecting a mere attention particle and the analysis as negation plus interrogative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p142/r6.anchor: وهذا تخريج بعيد. والظاهر أن ألا للعرض المضمن الحض على التقوى،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p108/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p108/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p108/r1.claim: The appeal that Pharaoh’s people be God-fearing asks whether they will avert His punishment by obeying Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p108/r1.anchor: ألا يصرفون عن أنفسهم عقوبة الله بطاعته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p226/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p226/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p226/r4.claim: The phrase alā yattaqūn simultaneously denies that they have reverence and commands them to be reverent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p226/r4.anchor: وقوله ألا يتقون معناه قل لهم فجمع في هذه العبارة من المعاني نفي التقوى عنهم وأمرهم بالتقوى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p226/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p226/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p226/r5.claim: Most readers have yattaqūn with yāʾ; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim, Ḥammād ibn Salama, and Abū Qilāba read tattaqūn with tāʾ, as a direct command to them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p226/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «يتقون» بالياء من تحت، وقرأ عبد الله بن مسلم وحماد بن سلمة

JISHUMI:v7p5342/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5342/r4.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v7p5342/r4.claim: The common reading has yāʾ in ألا يتقون, a third-person observation.
JISHUMI:v7p5342/r4.anchor: قراءة العامة: ألا يتقون بالياء على المعاينة،

JISHUMI:v7p5342/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5342/r5.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
JISHUMI:v7p5342/r5.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr reads with tāʾ, meaning tell them directly: will you not fear God?
JISHUMI:v7p5342/r5.anchor: وعن عبيد بن عمير بالتاء، أي: قل لهم ألا تتقون.

RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r6.claim: “The people of Pharaoh” is an explicative apposition to “the wrongdoers”; both expressions designate the same group.
RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r6.anchor: عطف بيان ، كأن القوم الظالمين وقوم فرعون لفظان يدلان على معنى واحد

BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r6.claim: “The people of Pharaoh” is appositional to “the people”; naming the people alone signals Pharaoh’s prominence among those judged.
BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r6.anchor: بدل من القوم والاقتصار على القوم للإيذان بشهرة أن فرعون أول داخل في الحكم.

BURSEVI:v6p192#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p192#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p192#3/r1.claim: The clause is a new sentence with no syntactic attachment; alā is an exhortation to act.
BURSEVI:v6p192#3/r1.anchor: استئناف لا محل له من الإعراب وألا تحضيض على الفعل أتبعه إرساله إليهم

BURSEVI:v6p192#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p192#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p192#3/r2.claim: Moses is sent to warn them, expressing astonishment at their injustice and aggression: will they not fear God and avert punishment through faith and obedience?
BURSEVI:v6p192#3/r2.anchor: أتبعه إرساله إليهم لإنذار وتعجيبا من غلوهم في الظلم وإفراطهم في العدوان أي ألا يخافون الله

STUDYQURAN:26:11/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:11/r1.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:26:11/r1.claim: One reading has God command Moses to ask the people whether they will not be reverent.
STUDYQURAN:26:11/r1.anchor: Some understand this verse to mean that God is commanding Moses to ask them, “Will you not be reverent?” (Q).

STUDYQURAN:26:11/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:11/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:26:11/r2.claim: Depending on the vocalization, the phrase can instead ask whether they will reverence God.
STUDYQURAN:26:11/r2.anchor: Depending on how the end of this verse is vocalized, it could also mean, “Will they not reverence Me?” (R).

STUDYQURAN:26:11/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:11/r3.speaker: some commentators (Ṭ)
STUDYQURAN:26:11/r3.claim: Reverence connotes mindfulness or caution; here it can mean being mindful of the Hereafter's punishment.
STUDYQURAN:26:11/r3.anchor: and thus some understand this verse to mean that they should be mindful of the punishment of the Hereafter (Ṭ).

TAB-FULL:v17p552/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p552/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p552/r1.claim: The second “people” specifies the first: the wicked people are Pharaoh’s disbelieving people, and the question asks whether they will fear God’s punishment for disbelief.
TAB-FULL:v17p552/r1.anchor: يعني الكافرين قوم فرعون، ونصب القوم الثاني ترجمة عن القوم الأول

TAB-FULL:v17p552/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p552/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p552/r2.claim: The implied command is “tell them: will they not fear?”; “tell them” is omitted because the context supplies it.
TAB-FULL:v17p552/r2.anchor: ومعنى الكلام قوم فرعون فقل لهم: ألا يتقون. وترك إظهار فقل لهم لدلالة الكلام عليه.

TAB-FULL:v17p552/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p552/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p552/r3.claim: The transmitted yāʾ form reflects narration before direct address; a tāʾ reading is also correct, as in the alternate forms at 3:12.
TAB-FULL:v17p552/r3.anchor: وإنما قيل: ألا يتقون بالياء، ولم يقل ألا تتقون بالتاء، لأن التنزيل كان قبل الخطاب

TABATABAI:26:10-13/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:10-13/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:10-13/r1.claim: The sequence of earlier prophets shows that Muhammad's people follow the same path and will face punishment; repeated story endings echo the opening rejection, console the Prophet, show his mission is not unprecedented, and implicitly warn his people.
TABATABAI:26:10-13/r1.anchor: ليظهر أن قوم النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم سائرون مسيرهم وسيردون موردهم

TABATABAI:26:10-13/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:10-13/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:10-13/r4.claim: The third-person wording is a rebuke delivered from afar; in the commissioning context it means Moses should tell them that his Lord reproaches their abandonment of piety.
TABATABAI:26:10-13/r4.anchor: بصيغة الغيبة، وهو توبيخ غيابي منه تعالى لهم

TABRISI:26:10-12/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:10-12/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم بن يسار وحماد بن سلمة
TABRISI:26:10-12/r3.claim: In a noncanonical reading, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim ibn Yasār and Ḥammād ibn Salama read the address with tāʾ: “Will you not be God-fearing?”
TABRISI:26:10-12/r3.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة عبد الله بن مسلم بن يسار وحماد بن سلمة ألا تتقون بالتاء

TABRISI:26:10-12/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:10-12/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:10-12/r4.claim: The tāʾ reading supplies an unspoken “say to them,” making the words Moses’ direct address to Pharaoh’s people.
TABRISI:26:10-12/r4.anchor: ومن قرأ ألا تتقون بالتاء فهو على إضمار القول أي فقل لهم ألا تتقون

TABRISI:26:10-12/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:10-12/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:10-12/r14.claim: The stories of earlier messengers console Muhammad and urge him to persevere, trusting that victory will come.
TABRISI:26:10-12/r14.anchor: ثم ذكر سبحانه أقاصيص رسله تسلية للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وتحريضا له على الصبر ثقة بنزول النصر

TABRISI:26:10-12/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:10-12/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:10-12/r16.claim: “Pharaoh’s people” is an explanatory apposition to “the unjust people.”
TABRISI:26:10-12/r16.anchor: ثم بين القوم الموصوفين بهذه الصفة فقال: { قوم فرعون } وهو عطف بيان

TABRISI:26:10-12/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:10-12/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:10-12/r17.claim: The reported third-person wording means, “Is it not time for them to fear?” and avoid God’s punishment through obedience.
TABRISI:26:10-12/r17.anchor: إنما قاله بالياء لأنه على الحكاية ومعناه أما آن لهم أن يتقوا ويصرفوا عن أنفسهم عقوبة الله بطاعته

TABRISI:26:10-12/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:10-12/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:10-12/r18.claim: Taqwā means avoiding reprehensible things by doing good; its root sense is to put a barrier between oneself and what one avoids.
TABRISI:26:10-12/r18.anchor: والتقوى مجانبة القبائح بفعل المحاسن وأصله صرف الأمر بحاجز بين الصارف وبينه

THALABI:v7p159#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p159#2/r3.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
THALABI:v7p159#2/r3.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr reads the verb with tāʾ, addressing Moses and Aaron's audience directly: “Will you not fear God?”
THALABI:v7p159#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ عبيد بن عمير بالتاء أي قل لهما: ألا تتقون؟

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p26/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p26/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p26/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says tattaqūn is valid because Moses was to address them; yat-taqūn is also valid because the revelation begins before direct address, as in 3:12.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p26/r1.anchor: قال الفراء: لو قرئ: {ألا تتقون} بالتاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p26/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p26/r2.speaker: أبو حاتم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p26/r2.claim: Stop after qawmu Firʿawn because its meaning is complete; the following words begin a new sentence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p26/r2.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم: قوله {قوم فرعون} وقف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p26/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p26/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p26/r3.claim: The question asks why they do not avert God's punishment by obeying Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p26/r3.anchor: ومعنى: {ألا يتقون} ألا يصرفون عن أنفسهم عقوبة الله بطاعته

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:10-11/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:10-11/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:10-11/r3.claim: Moses is told to ask whether they will not fear God and believe in Him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:10-11/r3.anchor: ألا يخافون الله سبحانه فيؤمنوا به

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p496/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p496/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p496/r3.claim: God commands Moses to go to the wrongdoers, Pharaoh’s people, and calls them to fear God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p496/r3.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {وإذ نادى ربك موسى أن ائت القوم الظالمين {10} قوم فرعون ألا يتقون {11} } [الشعراء: 10-11] ، أي: فليتقوا الله. قال موسى.

QASHANI:26:10-12/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:26:10-12/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:26:10-12/r2.claim: The warning invokes God's overwhelming force and wrath, which destroys and annihilates them.
QASHANI:26:10-12/r2.anchor: { ألا يتقون } قهري وبأسي بتدميرهم وإفنائهم

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:10/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:10/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:10/r1.claim: Moses faced a harder mission than Muhammad: he came from an enslaved people to summon Pharaoh, while Muhammad shared his audience’s status and faced less powerful opponents; Moses’s success encourages the Prophet and believers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:10/r1.anchor: Bu âyetler, o zor şartlarda Hz. Mûsâ nasıl başarılı olduysa Hz. Peygamber’in de öyle başarılı olacağına işaret etmekte, müminlere ümit ve cesaret vermektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:10/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:10/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:10/r2.claim: God calls Pharaoh’s people unjust because they enslaved Israelites, killed newborn boys when their population grew, and denied God’s existence and oneness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:10/r2.anchor: İşte bu tutumları yanında Allah’ın varlığını ve birliğini de tanımamaları sebebiyle Allah onları “zalim kavim” olarak nitelendirmektedir

BURHAN:v2p342/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p342/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p342/r5.claim: Moses' ألا يتقون means go to Pharaoh's people and command them to fear God.

BURHAN:v4p235/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p235/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p235/r1.claim: When interrogative hamza combines with negative lā, the question asserts the negated proposition: Pharaoh's people are not God-fearing.
BURHAN:v4p235/r1.anchor: والاستفهام اذا دخل على النفي افاد تحقيقا

ITQAN:v2p441#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p441#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p441#2/r3.claim: The other uses are exhortation and gentle invitation: both request an action, but the first is more insistent and both occur with verbs.
ITQAN:v2p441#2/r3.anchor: الثاني والثالث التحضيض والعرض ومعناهما طلب الشيء

DAMGHANI:v1p493/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p493/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p493/r9.claim: اتقوا can mean worship; Pharaoh's people are asked whether they will worship God.
DAMGHANI:v1p493/r9.anchor: اتقوا بمعنى اعبدوا قوله تعالى في سورة النحل أن أنذروا أنه لا اله إلا أنا فاتقون

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p219/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p219/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p219/r1.claim: Taqwā is relying on what creates a barrier between oneself and what one fears; the muttaqī guards against the thing feared.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p219/r1.anchor: التقوى : اعتماد المتقي ما يحصل به الحيلولة بينه وبين ما يكرهه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p219/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p219/r2.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p219/r2.claim: The author’s teacher says taqwā is more commendable than faith because faith may be mixed with other things, whereas taqwā is not.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p219/r2.anchor: وقال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله رضي الله عنه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p219/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p219/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p219/r3.claim: Taqwā is taking precautions; waraʿ is avoiding a doubtful matter, whose cause is conjectural, and restraining oneself from uncertain consequences.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p219/r3.anchor: ويقارب التقوى الورع إلا أن الفرق بينهما أن التقوى أخذ عدة والورع دفع شبهة

NAHHAS:v3p175/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p175/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p175/r1.anchor: بدل ( ألا يتقون ) لأنهم غيب عن المخاطبة

NAHHAS:v3p175/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p175/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p175/r2.claim: The third-person form is used because Pharaoh's people are absent from direct address; the second-person ألا تتقون is also possible as a command to tell them.
NAHHAS:v3p175/r2.anchor: لأنهم غيب عن المخاطبة ويجوز ألا تتقون بمعنى قل لهم

NAHHAS:v3p175/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p175/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p175/r3.claim: The shift to direct address can be compared with 3:12, where the Prophet is told to address the unbelievers directly.
NAHHAS:v3p175/r3.anchor: ومثله ﴿ قل للذين كفروا ستغلبون ﴾ بالتاء والياء

SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r1.claim: Qawma Firʿawn is apposition or explicative apposition to al-qawm al-ẓālimīn.
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r1.anchor: بدل أو عطف بيان للقوم الظالمين

SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r2.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ parses qawma Firʿawn as the object of tattaqūn in the address reading, or as a vocative.
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r2.anchor: إنه مفعول " تتقون " على قراءة من قرأ " تتقون "

SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r3.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r3.claim: The common reading uses third-person yattaqūna with an open n; the people of Pharaoh are meant and “punishment” is the omitted object.
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r3.anchor: العامة على الياء في " يتقون " وفتح النون، والمراد قوم فرعون

SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم ابن يسار وحماد وشقيق بن سلمة
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim ibn Yasār, Ḥammād, and Shaqīq ibn Salama read with second-person tāʾ, shifting address to rebuke them.
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r4.anchor: قرأ عبد الله بن مسلم ابن يسار وحماد وشقيق بن سلمة بالتاء من فوق

SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r5.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r5.claim: Another reading has third-person yaʾ and a kasra on n; this may be a present verb whose first-person object yāʾ is represented by the kasra.
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r5.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم " يتقون " بالياء من تحت وكسر النون. وفيها تخريجان

SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also parses it as yāʾ of address followed by the imperative ittaqūn, “O people, fear Me”; the author calls this remote.
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r6.anchor: جوزه الزمخشري أن تكون " يا " للنداء. و " اتقون " فعل أمر

SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r7.claim: The sentence can stand independently; al-Zamakhsharī also allows a circumstantial clause describing the wrongdoers as not fearing God or His punishment.
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r7.anchor: وفي هذه الجملة وجهان، أحدهما: أنها مستأنفة لا محل لها من الإعراب

SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats the clause as circumstantial from the pronoun in al-ẓālimīn; the Shaykh objects that qawma Firʿawn intervenes and that a pre-hamza element cannot govern what follows it.
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r8.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري أن تكون حالا من الضمير في الظالمين أي: يظلمون غير متقين

SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r9.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r9.claim: The Shaykh gives two syntactic objections to the circumstantial parse: an intervening unrelated phrase and the rule that what follows the interrogative hamza cannot be governed from before it.
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r9.anchor: خطأه الشيخ من وجهين، أحدهما: أنه يلزم منه الفصل بين الحال وعاملها

SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r10.claim: The apparent force of alā is an offer or exhortation; al-Zamakhsharī takes it as lā with an interrogative of denial, while another view makes it an attention particle.
SAMIN-DURR:26:11/r10.anchor: والظاهر أن " ألا " للعرض. وقال الزمخشري

ASAD-NOTES:26:10#n7/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:26:10#n7/r1.speaker: Zamakhshari and Razi
ASAD-NOTES:26:10#n7/r1.claim: Zamakhshari and Razi take the rhetorical question as a factual assertion that Pharaoh's people refuse to become conscious of God.
ASAD-NOTES:26:10#n7/r1.anchor: Zamakhshari and Razi understand this rhetorical question in the sense apparent in my rendering, namely, as a statement of fact.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p127/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p127/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم بن يسار وحماد بن سلمة
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p127/r1.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim ibn Yasār and Ḥammād ibn Salama read تتقون with direct second-person address; Ibn Jinnī supplies an implied فقل لهم, like سلام عليكم with an implied يقولون.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p127/r1.anchor: قرأ عبد الله بن مسلم بن يسار وحماد بن سلمة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r1.claim: قوم فرعون is explanatory apposition for القوم الظالمين, identifying them as exemplary in wrongdoing; the construction signals this meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r1.anchor: عطف بيان للقوم الظألمين جيء به للايذان بانهم علم في الظلم كان معنى القوم الظالمين

ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa parses قوم فرعون as a substitute for القوم الظالمين; Abu Hayyan prefers apposition for its rhetorical force.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء : بدل منه ورجح أبو حيان الأول بانه اقتضى لحق البلاغة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r3.claim: A possible construal includes Pharaoh himself in the people of Pharaoh, as Adam is included in the children of Adam.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يقال قوم فرعون شامل له شمول بني آدم آدم عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r4.claim: The phrase is circumstantial with an implied speech verb: send them, saying, 'Will they not fear?'
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r4.anchor: حال بتقدير القول أي ائتهم قائلا لهم ألا يتقون

ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم بن يسار
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r5.claim: Abd Allah ibn Muslim ibn Yasar, Shaqiq ibn Salama, Hammad ibn Salama, and Abu Qilaba read the verb in direct address; both direct address and third person are permissible after a command to tell someone.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن مسلم بن يسار وشقيق بن سلمة وحماد بن سلمة وأبو قلابة بتاء الخطاب

ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r6.claim: A reading with kasra on the nūn derives from تتقونني, dropping one of the two nūns and then the yā, with its kasra retained.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r6.anchor: وقريء بكسر النون مع الخطاب والغيبة والأصل بتقونني فحذفت إحدى النونين لاجتماع المثلين

ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r7.claim: Moses speaks this warning for God, comparable to 2:186, as if God said, 'Will you not fear Me?'
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r7.anchor: بطريق النيابة عنه عز وجل نظير ما قوله تعالى ( وإذا سألك عبادي عني فاني قريب )

ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats the phrase as a separate divine resumption after the sending command: it registers their shocking injustice and lack of fear of God's punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r8.anchor: وقال الزمخشري هو كلام مستأنف اتبعه عز وجل إرساله اليهم للانذار والتسجيل عليهم بالظلم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the direct-address reading is an apostrophe that confronts and rebukes them; Moses' public delivery makes the warning as if spoken in their presence.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r9.anchor: وقراءة الخطاب على طريقة الالتفات اليهم وجبههم وضرب وجوههم بالانكار والغضب عليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also construes the third-person form as a circumstantial clause attached to الظالمين, but Abu Hayyan calls this a grave error; the author finds the defense unconvincing.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r10.anchor: وقال أيضا : يحتمل أن يكون ( لايتقون ) حالا من الضمير في ( الظالمين ) أي يظلمون غير غير متقين الله تعالى وعقابه عز وجل فادخلت همزة الانكار

ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r11.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r11.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that this circumstantial analysis separates governor and complement with an intervening element and makes a pre-hamza element govern what follows; a response says the intervening matter is not foreign.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r11.anchor: وتعقبه أبو حيان بانه خطأ فاحش لأن فيه مع الفصل بين العامل والمعمول بالأجنبي

ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r12.claim: A distant analysis parses ألا as exhortation plus a dropped vocative يا and the imperative اتقون, but dropping both alifs is irregular; the apparent sense in all readings is exhortation to piety.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r12.anchor: فتكون ( ألا ) كلمة واحدة للعرض ويا ندائية سقطت الفها لالتقاء الساكنين وحذف المنادى

ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r13.claim: The apparent function of ألا in every reading is an exhortation that urges them to fear God.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64#2/r13.anchor: وأن الظاهر أن ألا للعرض المضمن الحض على التقوى في جميع القرءات

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r7.claim: “Pharaoh’s people” is an apposition or explanatory substitute; only his people are named because Pharaoh’s role is evident.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r7.anchor: بدل من الأول أو عطف بيان له، ولعل الاقتصار على القوم للعلم بأن فرعون

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r8.claim: The separate question follows Moses’s mission to warn, expressing amazement at their extreme wrongdoing and audacity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r8.anchor: استئناف أتبعه إرساله إليهم للإنذار تعجيبا له من إفراطهم في الظلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r9.claim: A tāʾ reading directly addresses and rebukes them; though absent, they are treated as present because the messenger conveys the address, intensifying the call to reflect and fear God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r9.anchor: وقرىء بالتاء على الالتفات إليهم زجرا لهم وغضبا عليهم، وهم وإن كان غيبا حينئذ

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r10.claim: A kasra on the nūn may dispense with the possessive yāʾ, or mean “O people, fear Me,” as in ألا يا اسجدوا.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r10.anchor: وقرىء بكسر النون اكتفاء بها عن ياء الإضافة، ويحتمل أن يكون بمعنى ألا يا ناس اتقون

BIQAI-FULL:v5p350/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p350/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p350/r1.claim: The people meant are Pharaoh’s people, deeply unjust through disbelief, wronging themselves, the Israelites, and other servants.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p350/r1.anchor: وظلم بني إسرائيل وغيرهم من العباد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p350/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p350/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p350/r2.claim: The question is an accusatory appeal for them to become God-fearing; it conveys severe anger, records their injustice, and marvels that long respite has only increased their stubbornness.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p350/r2.anchor: في سياق الإنكار عليهم , والإيذان بشديد الغضب منهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p350/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p350/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p350/r3.claim: Knowing that people resist what opposes their desires, the account anticipates Moses asking for divine help, in a manner compared with the complaint in 25:30.

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2752/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2752/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2752/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says Pharaoh pursued Moses with Haman at the head of an army of 1.7 million horses, none female.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2752/r1.anchor: السدي قال : خرج موسى وتبعهم فرعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r1.claim: Calling them oppressors signals why Moses is sent, primes him to learn who they are, and stirs indignation to reinforce obedience and make his address more forceful; it hints their oppression is notorious.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r1.anchor: إيماء إلى علة الإرسال . وفي هذا الإجمال توجيه نفس موسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r2.claim: Repeating قوم to specify Pharaoh's people adds emphasis; Ibn Ashur cites Jarir's repeated vocative يا تيم تيم عدي as a parallel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r2.anchor: وفي تكرير كلمة { قوم } موقع من التأكيد فلم يقل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r3.claim: Their oppression includes wronging themselves through idolatry and violating others' rights by enslaving and persecuting the Israelites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r3.anchor: والظلم يعم أنواعه ، فمنها ظلمهم أنفسهم بعبادة ما لا يستحق العبادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r4.claim: The Qur'an uses ظلم for both injustice against others and associationism against oneself, with examples at 2:114 and 6:82.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r4.anchor: وتقدم استعماله في المعنيين مرارا في ضد العدل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r5.claim: The account omits the opening call in 20:12–23 because this passage focuses on the mission to Pharaoh and his rejection; the Ta Ha account instead expands on Moses' honor and prophethood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r5.anchor: قد عدل هنا عن ذكر ما ابتدىء به نداء موسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r6.claim: The command means Moses is to go and convey the message; the compressed wording is explained by the later command to go together to Pharaoh and speak.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r6.anchor: والإتيان المأمور به هو ذهابه لتبليغ الرسالة إليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r7.claim: On one parse, ألا consists of interrogative hamza plus negative لا; the question rejects the absence of fear and expresses Moses' astonishment.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r8.claim: As a standalone explanatory question, it shows their entrenched oppression and prepares Moses to persist despite their likely rejection; he knew their abuses from growing up among them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p103/r8.anchor: مستأنفة استئنافا بيانيا لأنه لما أمره بالإتيان إليهم لدعوتهم ووصفهم بالظالمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p105/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p105/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p105/r1.claim: A second analysis takes ألا as one particle of urging, making the sentence an explanation of ائت: tell them, in effect, 'Will you not fear?'
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p105/r1.anchor: هي أداة العرض والتحضيض فتكون جملة : { ألا يتقون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p105/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p105/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p105/r2.claim: The command can be reported by meaning rather than exact wording, as in the verse where Jesus describes what God commanded him to say.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p105/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p105/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p105/r3.claim: Fear and caution are the sense of اتقاء here; the implicit object is the consequences of their wrongdoing, as in the earlier usage in 8:56.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p105/r3.anchor: والاتقاء : الخوف والحذر ، وحذف متعلق فعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p105/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p105/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p105/r4.claim: The description of Pharaoh's people teaches Moses to begin by calling them away from injustice and toward piety.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p105/r4.anchor: من إجراء وصف الظلم وعدم التقوى على قوم فرعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p105/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p105/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p105/r5.claim: Ibn Ashur points back to the mention of Moses at 2:51 and to the account of Pharaoh at 7:103.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p105/r5.anchor: وذكر موسى تقدم عند قوله تعالى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r3.claim: With kasra on the nūn, alā yattaqūni means “will they not fear Me?”; one nūn is deleted where two meet and the yāʾ is omitted, its kasra remaining.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r3.anchor: قرىء : ( ألا يتقون ) بكسر النون ، بمعنى : ألا يتقونني : فحذفت النون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r4.claim: The question may be an independent remark after Moses is sent, registering their wrongdoing and expressing amazement at their oppression and lack of fear of God's punishment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r4.anchor: هو كلام مستأنف أتبعه عز وجل إرساله إليهم للإنذار ، والتسجيل عليهم بالظلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r5.claim: Alternatively, yattaqūna is a circumstantial clause describing the wrongdoers as unjust without fearing God or His punishment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r5.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون { لا يتقون } حالا من الضمير في الظالمين ، أي : يظلمون غير متقين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r6.claim: The second-person reading alā tattaqūna shifts to direct address, confronting and angrily rebuking Pharaoh's people; the author illustrates it with an accuser turning to scold the culprit present.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r6.anchor: وأما من قرأ : ألا تتقون . على الخطاب . فعلى طريقة الالتفات إليهم ، وجبههم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r7.claim: Addressing absent recipients during Moses's private colloquy is like speaking in their presence because Moses will convey it; the wording urges him toward piety and gives believers lessons from verses about unbelievers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r7.anchor: إجراء ذلك في تكليم المرسل إليهم في معنى إجرائه بحضرتهم وإلقائه إلى مسامعهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r8.claim: Another analysis of the yāʾ reading with kasra takes it as alā yā nāsi ittaqūn, “People, will you not fear Me?”, compared with the address in 2:34.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r8.anchor: وفي { ألا يتقون } بالياء وكسر النون وجه آخر ، وهو أن يكون المعنى : ألا يا ناس اتقون

MUQATIL:26:10-15/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:10-15/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:10-15/r3.claim: The people of Pharaoh were in Egypt, and Pharaoh’s name was Fitus.

MUQATIL:26:10-15/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:10-15/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:10-15/r4.claim: “Will they not be God-conscious?” means “Will they not worship God?”
MUQATIL:26:10-15/r4.anchor: يعنى ألا يعبدون الله عز وجل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#7/r1.claim: “Pharaoh's people” is an explanatory apposition, glossing the oppressive people as Pharaoh's people; both expressions denote the same group.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#7/r1.anchor: عليهم عطف البيان كأن معنى القوم الظالمين وترجمته قوم فرعون

NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#7/r2.claim: This is an urging: go to them as an admonisher, for it is time they became Godfearing.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#7/r2.anchor: أى ائتهم زاجرا فقد آن لهم أن يتقوا وهى كلمة حث وإغراء

NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#7/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#7/r3.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is circumstantial of the pronoun in “the wrongdoers”: they oppress while heedless of God and His punishment, with the interrogative hamza applied to the circumstance.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#7/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أنه حال من الضمير فى الظالمين أى يظلموا غير متقين الله وعقابه

QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r5.claim: “Pharaoh’s people” is an apposition specifying the unjust people.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r5.anchor: ف { قوم } بدل ومعنى { ألا يتقون } ألا يخافون عقاب الله؟

QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r6.claim: The question asks whether they fear God’s punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r6.anchor: ومعنى { ألا يتقون } ألا يخافون عقاب الله؟

QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r7.claim: The command to approach the unjust people and the question about fearing God imply that they do not fear Him and that Moses was to call them to piety.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r7.anchor: وقيل هذا من الإيماء إلى الشيء لأنه أمره أن يأتي القوم الظالمين، ودل قوله: { يتقون } على أنهم لا يتقون

QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r8.claim: The third-person form suits people absent at the moment of address; direct second-person address would also be valid, as in 3:12.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r8.anchor: وقيل: المعنى قل لهم { ألا تتقون } وجاء بالياء لأنهم غيب وقت الخطاب

QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r9.speaker: عبيد بن عمير وأبو حازم
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r9.claim: They read with two tāʾs, making the sense a direct command to tell Pharaoh’s people, “Will you not be mindful?”
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r9.anchor: وقد قرأ عبيد بن عمير وأبو حازم { ألا تتقون } بتاءين أي قل لهم { ألا تتقون }
